sources.label: GR
sources.role: orbifold-existence endpoint
sources.source_status: Published in Advances in Mathematics 482 (2025), 110546; theorem numbering audited in pinned arXiv v1
results_used: Section 2.1, printed/PDF page 4, and Section 2.2, page 6: Uniqueness of the positive ribbon structure in the pseudounitary setting, and the physical VOA twist exp(2*pi*i*h_M). Positivity of nonvacuum conformal weights places the VOA module category in this setting.

Theorem 2.2 and the following paragraph, printed/PDF page 7: The actual twisted-module category is obtained from the parent algebra Res_(V^G)V, and its equivariantization is Mod(V^G); algebra automorphisms match the actual group action.

Theorem 3.1, printed/PDF page 11, and the decomposition immediately after equation (3.1), page 12: For holomorphic V with strongly rational V^G, the actual twisted category is Vec_G^omega, with its actual automorphism grading and centralizer-character decomposition.
Section 3.2, printed/PDF page 13: The ribbon twist of a centralizer-labelled simple [g,chi] is chi(g)/chi(1), used after ribbon compatibility to obtain ground-character eligibility.
sources.scope_check: The relative equivalence retains the specified tensor copy of Rep(E) arising from the parent VOA. Positivity makes that braided equivalence ribbon. Centralizer relabelling rephases each full-module implementer by one scalar; it does not permit separate ground/oscillator rephasings or independently chosen origins for different conjugacy classes.

sources.label: BK
sources.title: Twisted Modules over Lattice Vertex Algebras
sources.role: Twisted lattice defect dimension, fixed-momentum fibers and Fock decomposition
sources.checked_version: arXiv:math/0402315v3, 31 March 2004; 18 pages; internal manuscript date 19 February 2004
sources.source_status: Published as a chapter in Lie Theory and Its Applications in Physics V, World Scientific (2004), pp. 3-26. Numbering here is pinned to arXiv v3.
results_used: Equation (4.53), printed page 16 / PDF page 16: The squared defect dimension is the order of the relevant finite nondegenerate quotient.
Proposition 4.3 and equations (4.54)-(4.55), printed page 16 / PDF page 16: The twisted module is induced from its oscillator-vacuum subspace and has the corresponding symmetric Fock factor.
Lemma 4.7, printed page 17 / PDF page 17: Momentum fibers are translated by projected lattice vectors and carry the irreducible finite defect representation.

Theorem 4.2 and Remark 4.4, printed page 18 / PDF page 18: Classification and explicit Heisenberg-module decomposition S(hat h_sigma^+) tensor e^(lambda_0) C[pi_0 Q] tensor C^d(sigma). The source uses plus for negative-mode creation operators.
Equation (4.19) and Proposition 4.1, printed/PDF page 9: The lift phase equals one on the fixed sublattice in the standard-lift convention used for the zero-shift momentum decomposition.

Definition 4.1(iii), printed/PDF page 15, together with Theorem 4.2, page 18: For an even lattice, twisted simple modules are parametrized by (Q^*/Q)^sigma. For the even unimodular lattice this is a singleton, giving the uniqueness used to transport physical twisted modules under an actual normalizer.
sources.scope_check: For the even unimodular lattice and standard lift, the momentum shift is zero. The claim that weight four consists only of the zero-momentum oscillator-vacuum fiber also uses rho_g=4 and positive definiteness. The dimension 2^16 is derived independently from KRR (A.2.5), not asserted for arbitrary unrelated lattices.

sources.label: BDM
sources.title: Twisted Sectors for Tensor Product Vertex Operator Algebras Associated to Permutation Groups
sources.role: Permutation-twisted module construction and swap ground-weight comparison
sources.source_status: Published in Communications in Mathematical Physics 227 (May 2002), 349-384; cited numbering audited in pinned arXiv v2
results_used: Equation (3.6), printed page 14 / PDF page 14: the transformed single-factor conformal field, including its central-charge correction.

Theorem 3.9, printed/PDF pages 22-23, explicit formula on page 23: L_g(0)=L(0)/k+(k^2-1)c/(24k) for the k-cycle-twisted module constructed from a V-module; c is the central charge of one factor V, not of V tensor k.
Theorem 4.4, printed/PDF pages 26-27: equivalence of ordinary V-modules with ordinary k-cycle-twisted tensor-product modules, preserving irreducibility.
sources.scope_check: For a holomorphic CFT-type seed U of charge c_seed, its unique ordinary module has ground weight zero. The swap of U tensor U therefore has twisted ground weight c_seed/16, at least 8 when c_seed is at least 128. The theorem is not restricted to lattice VOAs. It supplies the twisted spectrum; it does not itself assert existence or unitarity of the holomorphic orbifold extension.

sources.label: vEMS
sources.title: Construction and Classification of Holomorphic Vertex Operator Algebras
sources.role: General-central-charge type-zero cyclic holomorphic orbifold theorem and positivity hypotheses
sources.checked_version: arXiv:1507.08142v3, 28 November 2017, 22:35:42 UTC; 37 pages; Section 5 numbering is version-specific
sources.source_status: Published in Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik (Crelle's Journal) 759 (2020), 61-99; publisher gives online publication date 16 November 2017; cited numbering audited in pinned arXiv v3
results_used: Theorems 5.1-5.2, printed/PDF pages 11-12: rationality and C2-cofiniteness of the cyclic fixed algebra, and its n^2 simple modules W^(i,j) from twisted-sector eigenspaces.
Theorem 5.11 and the following definition, printed/PDF pages 17-18: rho_g lies in (1/n^2)Z and the automorphism type is t=n^2 rho_g modulo n.

Theorem 5.16, printed/PDF pages 20-21: a simple, rational, C2-cofinite, holomorphic CFT-type parent with positive conformal weights for all nonvacuum W^(i,j) admits the isotropic-subgroup extension; H=H^perp gives a holomorphic extension, retaining these finiteness properties and self-contragredience.
Type-zero specialization after Theorem 5.16, printed page 21 / PDF page 21: the compatible labels have fusion group Z_n times Z_n, quadratic form ij/n, and holomorphic extension direct_sum_i W^(i,0).
sources.scope_check: Section 5 applies to general central charge, independently of the later charge-24 classification. Apply it to the parent U tensor U, whose charge is 2*c_seed. BDM gives type 4*rho_swap=c_seed/4 modulo 2, hence zero for c_seed=128*2^k. The antisymmetric untwisted module has positive weight because the unique weight-zero vector is swap-invariant; both twisted eigenspaces have weight at least c_seed/16, so all three nonvacuum fixed-algebra modules satisfy the required positivity. This theorem establishes the strongly rational holomorphic extension, not unitarity; preservation of the primary gap is a separate low-weight argument.

sources.label: St
sources.title: Lectures on Chevalley Groups
sources.role: Exact finite-field presentation used for the genuine Cartesian GL(7,2) lift
sources.checked_version: Original Yale University lecture notes, 1967; notes prepared by John Faulkner and Robert Wilson; acknowledgement dated June 1968; 284 PDF pages
sources.source_status: Yale University lecture notes. The consulted source is the original typewritten scan; no later edited edition or its pagination is substituted.
results_used: Section 6, Theorem 9 and its following Example, printed page 72 / PDF page 79: The finite-field presentation of SL(n,k) for n at least 3 by elementary root generators and the stated additivity, chain-commutator and commuting relations. Specializing to k=F_2 and n=7 gives GL(7,2)=SL(7,2).
sources.scope_check: The presentation covers all required shared-index relators over F_2 and imposes no field-size-greater-than-four restriction here. Verifying the particular lattice lifts against every relator uses the separate common-support argument on at most four tensor positions. The source alone supplies neither those lift equalities nor a splitting of the entire lattice normalizer.

sources.source_status: Published in Nagoya Mathematical Journal 176 (2004), 19–98. The official publisher PDF is the consulted version.
results_used: Section 3, printed page 35 / PDF page 17: L_n(2) is the finite linear group acting on its natural n-dimensional GF(2)-module U, and U^[i] denotes the i-th exterior power.
Lemma 3.2, printed page 36 / PDF page 18: H^1(L_n(2),U^[i]) vanishes except at (n,i)=(3,1),(3,2),(4,2). Hence the n=7, i=2 and i=5 cases used for the two exterior-power summands vanish.
sources.scope_check: This is the directly consulted published restatement, attributed there to Jones–Parshall [JP76]. No claim is made to have checked the original 1976 chapter. It concerns ordinary cohomology of the finite group, so no rational algebraic-group comparison is assumed.

sources.label: CGP
sources.title: On the 1-cohomology of SL(n,K) on the dual of its adjoint module
sources.role: H^1 vanishing for the endomorphism-quotient summand
sources.checked_version: arXiv:2502.11808v2, 16 December 2025; 24 pages. The exact consulted PDF has the internal title-page date 18 December 2025.
sources.source_status: The consulted source is an arXiv preprint, version 2. No journal publication is asserted.
results_used: Section 1.1, printed/PDF page 2: The trace pairing identifies the dual adjoint module A_n^* with Mat_n(K)/<I> as an SL(n,K)-module.
Theorem 1.4, printed/PDF page 4: For n>3 and every field K, H^1(SL(n,K),A_n^*) is isomorphic to Der(K). Applying this to n=7 and K=F_2 gives zero.
Section 1, equation (1), printed/PDF page 1, and Section 2, equation (2), page 5: The source uses right conjugation and ordinary abstract-group right 1-cocycles.
sources.scope_check: The application uses the stated all-field n>3 theorem, not an older large-field variant. Conversion from the source right-module convention to the chosen left-action convention must be explicit. This entry does not itself prove the action on the relative-equivalence torsor or its uniqueness.
